title: Non-Hermitian Quantum Nonlinear Optics with Single Photons
authors: Samuel Napoli, Andrea Zappalá, Franco Nori, Salvatore Savasta, Daniele Lamberto
abstract: Quantum nonlinear optics seeks to harness strong photon-photon interactions for scalable quantum technologies, although dissipative losses still pose a major barrier to near-unity conversion efficiency. Here, we bridge non-Hermitian physics with the quantum nonlinear domain by exploiting perfect absorption to identify and optimize few-photon nonlinear processes. We theoretically investigate two circuit QED systems, operating in the light-matter ultrastrong coupling regime. The first (i) enables simultaneous two-atom excitations by single photons, while the second (ii) realizes the strong coupling between a single-photon and a two-photon Fock states. We demonstrate that, since the strong optical nonlinearities cause quantum spectral features to emerge already at the level of linear response theory, the perfect absorption condition in $|S_{11}|$ enables near-deterministic single-photon down-conversion into (i) a qubit-qubit-correlated pair and (ii) a two-photon pair. We show that the conversion efficiency can be systematically optimized through experimentally accessible parameters, both linked to the emergence of Hermitian subspaces within the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. These findings position non-Hermitian engineering as a broadly applicable route to optimizing quantum devices at the single-photon level, even beyond circuit-QED platforms.
summary: This paper pioneers the use of non-Hermitian physics, specifically perfect absorption, to overcome dissipation barriers in quantum nonlinear optics. By analyzing circuit QED systems operating in the ultrastrong coupling regime, the authors show how to engineer near-deterministic single-photon down-conversion into correlated multi-photon pairs. This establishes a powerful new route for optimizing quantum devices using non-Hermitian engineering principles.
main_problem: To develop scalable quantum technologies by harnessing strong photon-photon interactions while overcoming dissipative losses inherent in quantum nonlinear optics.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that exploiting perfect absorption conditions allows for near-deterministic single-photon down-conversion into correlated multi-photon pairs, even when realistic dissipation is present.
method: They bridge non-Hermitian physics with QNLO by analyzing the system's response using input-output theory and identifying optimal operating points via spectral analysis.
model_or_system: The study investigates two circuit QED systems involving qubits coupled to a resonator, modeled using generalized Dicke Hamiltonians in the light-matter ultrastrong coupling regime. The analysis focuses on effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians derived from input-output theory.
key_observables: Near-deterministic single-photon down-conversion efficiency ($\eta$), reflection coefficient $|S_{11}|$, and emission spectra $	ilde{S}_{q,1}(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Ultrastrong coupling regime (USC), perfect absorption condition in $|S_{11}|$, detuning ($\Delta\omega$), and experimentally accessible parameters governing loss rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the weak-excitation approximation for some parts, but crucially shows optimization is possible even with realistic dissipation present.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit QED setup (Fig. 1), show spectral features like avoided level crossings related to PA/zeros ($	ilde{\Omega}_{\pm}$), and plot conversion efficiencies ($\eta$) versus drive frequency or detuning.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework connecting PA to QNLO, then analyzing specific circuit QED setups (two-atom excitation, single-photon to two-photon conversion) using input-output theory and spectral mapping.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it directly applies non-Hermitian physics concepts (like PA and Hermitian subspaces) to optimize quantum light sources at the fundamental single-photon level within a cavity QED platform.
